summary: The mixed-timer receipt decided the point positively and forced a correction: with the leader on a 50ms lease and the other voters on a 20ms election timeout, a competing leader appeared 21ms after the partition and the cut-off leader went on confirming — ten confirmations followed the appearance of a leader one term ahead — while the uniform control saw no competing leader during its confirmation window at all. I therefore corrected the account I had recorded earlier rather than merely extending it. The child question's claim is now asserted for per-node timings and the parent VerifyLeader account is revised with that receipt joined to its own, so the stale-read basis the documented read pattern depends on is witnessed instead of argued — with the honest boundary kept: uniform configurations still close the window first, as twelve earlier trials and the source path show, so the exposure depends on whether a cluster's nodes share their timer settings, an environmental condition the library permits rather than enforces. I cleared the pause on the child question, recorded the knowledge uses at their exact revisions, and kept the counterevidence visible: the overlap needs differing timers, no application read is served so the witness is about the confirmation rather than a delivered value, the competing leader's appearance is only known within the 2ms poll, and the mixed witness was a single trial. Because that last point is the only remaining measurement, I also extended the same probe to twenty mixed trials and two controls in this same submission, declared both branches as comparisons so the observed rate is readable from the outcome either way, and kept it as a new child question about frequency rather than folding it into an answered one; my local dry run of that extension showed the overlap in all twenty mixed trials, with the competing leader appearing between 14ms and 44ms and between two and fifteen confirmations following it, against no overlap in either control.
